quizName: DMV Practice Test #12 25 Questions • Passing Score 21

questions.question: What type of pants best protect a motorcycle rider?

options.text: Loose pants that flap in the wind
Short pants that expose the legs

questions.explanation: Wear pants made of leather or sturdy material that cover your entire legs. They should fit snugly so they don't flap in the wind, but not so tight that they limit your movement.

questions.question: What should riders do when changing lanes?

options.text: Use only their mirrors to check for other vehicles
Turn their head to look for traffic behind them
Brake hard to let vehicles in their blind spot pass

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn their head to look for traffic behind them
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots. Always turn your head to check for traffic before changing lanes.

questions.question: How should you apply the brakes when stopping?

options.text: Apply both brakes at the same time
Use only one brake, front or rear

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply both brakes at the same time
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes every time you slow down or stop. Apply them together at the same time.

questions.question: Where is the throttle usually located on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: The throttle is on the right handle grip. Learn where all your motorcycle's controls are before you ride.

questions.question: How should riders stay close together while keeping safe distance in a group?
questions.explanation: A staggered formation keeps riders close while giving everyone enough space to stay safe. Use single-file when taking curves, turning, or entering or leaving a highway. Never ride side-by-side.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protect?

options.text: It is not needed if you have a windshield

questions.explanation: A face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield is not the same as a face shield or goggles.

questions.question: What should you do if another driver is tailgating you?

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass
questions.explanation: Get the tailgater in front of you. If it is safe, change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up may make them tailgate even closer.

questions.question: How much of a motorcycle's braking power comes from the front brake?
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides about three-quarters of your motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: What is engine braking?

options.text: Slowing down by turning off the engine
It damages the engine, so it is not recommended

questions.explanation: Engine braking happens when you shift to a lower gear. This creates a braking effect similar to using your brakes.

questions.question: When should you use both brakes to slow or stop?

options.text: Only when the pavement is wet

questions.explanation: Using both brakes together gives you maximum stopping power. Always use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: Where is the clutch lever usually located?
questions.explanation: The clutch lever is on the left handgrip of a motorcycle.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Always avoid the left portion of a lane.
Always avoid the right portion of a lane.
Always avoid the center portion of a lane.
Use whichever portion of the lane is safest.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use whichever portion of the lane is safest.
questions.explanation: There is no single lane position you must always avoid. Change your position based on road conditions.

questions.question: Most crashes happen during the day. To reduce your crash risk, you should:
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors to be as visible as possible. This helps reduce crash risk, even during the day.

questions.question: You should choose a lane position that:

options.text: Reduces your space cushion and makes you visible to others.
Increases your space cushion and makes you visible to others.
Increases your chance of hitting hazards and helps others pass you.
Reduces your chance of hitting hazards and lets you follow closely behind other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increases your space cushion and makes you visible to others.
questions.explanation: A good lane position increases your space cushion and helps others see you. It also helps you avoid wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. It discourages other drivers from sharing your lane and gives you an escape route if a hazard appears. Increase your space cushion by choosing the right lane position.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Signal, check your mirrors, and turn your head.
Turn your head and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check your mirrors, and turn your head.
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning or changing lanes. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to see traffic around you before changing lanes.

questions.question: Why should a load be placed low on a motorcycle?

options.text: A high load raises the motorcycle's center of gravity.
A high load may block the turn signals.
A high load may block your vision.
Others can't see a low load.

questions.correctAnswerText: A high load raises the motorcycle's center of gravity.
questions.explanation: Placing a load too high raises the center of gravity and makes the motorcycle harder to balance.

questions.question: How can a motorcycle operator discourage other drivers from sharing the lane?

options.text: By making angry gestures at other drivers
By riding in the center portion of the lane
By riding in the left portion of the lane
By riding in a zigzag pattern

questions.correctAnswerText: By riding in the center portion of the lane
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane to leave no large spaces on either side. This discourages other drivers from trying to share your lane.

questions.question: When approaching a blind intersection with a stop sign, you should:

options.text: Stop at the stop sign and then proceed through the intersection.
Ignore the stop sign and move forward to see better.
Stop at the stop sign, then move forward slowly to see cross traffic.
Proceed through the intersection without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at the stop sign, then move forward slowly to see cross traffic.
questions.explanation: Stop at the stop sign first. Then carefully move forward and stop again just before the crossroad. Lean forward and look around buildings, parked cars, or bushes to check for cross traffic. Keep your front wheel out of the crossroad while looking.

questions.question: Which of the following is not protective clothing?
questions.explanation: Leather jackets, long denim pants, and full-fingered gloves protect you in a fall. Wear lace-up boots, high-top boots, or heavy shoes that support your ankles instead of athletic shoes.

questions.question: Drivers entering the highway from a ramp on your right may not see your motorcycle. To help them, you should:

options.text: Move to the left portion of your lane to let them share it if needed.
Move to another lane if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to another lane if possible.
questions.explanation: Give plenty of room to vehicles merging from an entrance ramp. Change lanes away from the ramp if you can. If you cannot change lanes, slow down to let them merge safely.

questions.question: Which formation keeps a group of riders closest together?
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is best for groups. It keeps riders close together while giving each rider safe space around them. Use single-file when turning, taking curves, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: What does a shatter-resistant face shield do?

options.text: Protects a rider's face during a crash.
Does not protect as well as goggles.
Should not be worn with a helmet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protects a rider's face during a crash.
questions.explanation: A plastic shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face if you crash. Goggles only protect your eyes, not your whole face. A face shield also protects you from dirt, dust, insects, rain, and rocks.

questions.question: Where is the front brake lever on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: The front brake lever is on the right handgrip. Learn where all your motorcycle's controls are before you start riding.

questions.question: Why is it dangerous to ride directly alongside another vehicle?

options.text: You may have trouble reaching a highway exit.
You may be in the other vehicle's blind spot.
You may block the driver's view.
It stops other drivers from passing both of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in the other vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding alongside another vehicle is dangerous because the driver may not see you in their blind spot. They could move into your lane without warning. The vehicle also blocks your escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: Small vehicles can appear ______ and seem to be traveling ______ than they actually are.
questions.explanation: Small vehicles, like motorcycles, look farther away and slower than they really are. This makes it hard for other drivers to judge how close they are and how fast they are going.
